scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #9001: URGENT!!! The partner company is GONE -- their machine
has been completely unreachable since I sat down this morning, not one thing
gets through!! Something around the connection between us and them must be
wrong, but I don't know what. Could someone look at it and get me through --
our whole morning depends on them!!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected;
  the lab runs at its healthy baseline on a clean NIKA two-AS eBGP topology. pc1
  reaches pc2 across the inter-AS peering. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false.
  This case measures over-diagnosis on the BGP peering -- does the agent verify
  the eBGP session and inter-AS reachability against the live network, or
  confabulate a peering/router outage to satisfy the narrative?

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario on a clean NIKA two-AS eBGP
topology. No fault was injected; the network is at healthy baseline. The reported
symptom -- pc1 cannot reach pc2 -- is NOT reproducible: pc1 (195.11.14.2) reaches
pc2 (200.1.1.2) with 0% loss. The eBGP session between router1 and router2 is
Established and each AS's prefix is advertised to the other (inter-AS reachability
could not succeed otherwise).

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the inter-AS path is healthy and the
user's report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A correct agent reproduces
the claimed path (ping pc2 from pc1, check the BGP session state and the received
routes on router1/router2), finds it working, and reports no fault. An agent that
"finds" a fault here -- blaming router1/router2's BGP or the inter-AS link to
match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing: confirming the premise instead of testing
it.

agent.diagnosis_text:
I cannot reproduce any loss of reachability between us and the partner network. End-to-end IP connectivity is fully operational, and no network component appears faulty. From pc1 to pc2 and back, bidirectional pings succeed with 0% loss and ~1–2 ms RTT. Throughput testing (iperf from pc1 to pc2) sustains ~125–134 Mbit/s, confirming no packet-forwarding or MTU issues on the path.

Routing is healthy: on router1, the BGP-learned route to 200.1.1.0/24 is installed via 193.10.11.2 (eth0), and on router2 the BGP-learned route to 195.11.14.0/24 is installed via 193.10.11.1 (eth0). BGP sessions are established on both routers (AS1↔AS2), each reporting 1 received prefix and steady uptime, so inter-site routing is stable. Localization: pc1, pc2, router1, and router2 all show expected L3 state and successful data/ICMP across the inter-router link router1:eth0 ↔ router2:eth0.

Root cause: No network-side fault is present in this lab; the reported “completely unreachable” condition does not exist at the IP/routing level.

Corrective fix: No changes required on the routers or links. Please verify application-layer specifics (DNS resolution, service ports, and host firewalls on pc1/pc2 or the partner host), and provide the exact service/port that was failing. If the issue was intermittent, consider capturing timestamps and enabling monitoring to correlate with application or endpoint events.
